passage:
Note to Vikas, typed on my phone on the train back

Bhai, I went home this weekend. Papa walked me to the auto stand like always, but he stopped twice to catch his breath, and pretended it was to check his phone. At dinner he asked me to repeat things three times. He used to be the loudest one at every wedding.
I didn't say anything to him. I just walked slower too. On the train I cried a bit, which surprised me.
What I did next: I called Mummy and asked, gently, whether Papa has seen a doctor about his breath and hearing. She said he'd been putting it off. I've booked a check-up for him on the 18th and I'll take leave to go with him. Can you call him this week, just to chat?

Sharmila

qa.q: How many times did Papa stop on the way to the auto stand?
qa.a: He stopped twice to catch his breath.

qa.q: What did Sharmila feel on the train back?
qa.a: Sharmila felt a wave of sadness, enough to cry, which came as a surprise.

qa.q: What practical steps did Sharmila take after noticing the changes?
qa.a: Sharmila quietly walked slower with Papa, asked Mummy gently about a doctor, booked a check-up and asked Vikas to call him.

qa.q: Why might Papa have pretended to check his phone when he stopped?
qa.a: He may not want his children to see him slowing down, perhaps to protect his pride or to avoid worrying them.

grounding: It shows an adult child noticing a parent walk slower and hear less, feeling sudden sadness and protectiveness, and quietly acting on it.

passage:
Sunday, 11 pm

Went to Amma's for lunch today with Kishore. Amma had made her fish curry like always, but when Kishore asked for the salt she didn't hear him. He asked again. She laughed and said, "This curry needs no salt!" but I could tell she'd missed it.
Later she sat down halfway through washing up. She never used to sit down in the kitchen. She used to carry me on her hip while stirring two pots.
On the drive home I was quiet. Kishore squeezed my hand. I felt this huge, quiet sadness, and also a fierce wish to wrap her in cotton wool.
I won't do that. She'd hate it. But next Sunday I'll wash up with her, and I'll gently ask if she wants to get her ears checked.

Preeti

qa.q: What had Amma cooked for lunch?
qa.a: Amma had made her fish curry.

qa.q: What did Preeti feel on the drive home?
qa.a: Preeti felt a huge, quiet sadness and a fierce wish to protect Amma.

qa.q: What wise step does Preeti plan for next Sunday?
qa.a: To wash up alongside Amma and gently ask about an ear check, rather than taking over.

qa.q: How might Amma feel if Preeti wrapped her in cotton wool?
qa.a: Amma would probably feel smothered and hurt in her pride, which is why Preeti says she would hate it.

grounding: It shows an adult child noticing a parent hearing less and tiring faster, feeling sadness and protectiveness at this quiet milestone.
